definition.text: Reliability, as a cross-cutting concern, is keeping a unit of agent work correct under failure and retry across the whole journey, not a property of one call. This repo's own dispatch contract already names the boundary reliability has to make safe to exercise: one unit must specify "the request shape, the result shape, cancellation semantics, timeout and budget enforcement, partial-result handling, and what a failure returns" (F-b5-03). This repo's own architecture already names the state a reliable retry needs and records it as unbuilt: a "dispatch-level retry attempt - one transparent re-try of a single dispatch call, its cause class, its backoff and its attempt number" (A-state-dispatch-level-retry-attempt-one-transparent-re-try-of-a-single-dispatch-call-its-cause-class-its-backoff-and-its-attempt-number), whose own status is marked gap: its home_today field states plainly that today there are three separate dispatch implementations and no shared contract between them for what a retry does.

evidence.quote: the request shape, the result shape, cancellation semantics, timeout and budget enforcement, partial-result handling, and what a failure returns
dispatch-level retry attempt - one transparent re-try of a single dispatch call, its cause class, its backoff and its attempt number

standards.role: the wire-level convention this repo's own target table names as the standard for the Idempotency capability: an idempotency key travels with the request so a repeated delivery is recognized as the same one, not a fresh execution (F-b3-16).
standards.covers: does not by itself supply a lease, a payload-fingerprint conflict check, or a retention window -- cap-idempotency's own contract adds those. This repo's own adapter today implements only the bare key: 'key on the wire, no lease' (F-b3-16), which is weaker than the fingerprint-and-lease shape production guidance describes (see landscape and gaps).

evidence.text: This repo's own target table names the idempotency-key convention as Idempotency's standard, 'key on the wire, no lease' as today's adapter, and 'any keyed lease store' as the swap candidate.

evidence.quote: key on the wire, no lease

standards.role: supplies the typed failure a retry decision has to read before it decides whether to retry at all -- a status alone is not enough to say what caused it.
standards.covers: does not itself define retry policy, backoff or idempotency; it only standardizes the shape of the failure that reliability logic consumes.

evidence.text: Proposed: typed RFC 9457 error bodies commonly support classifying statuses like 429/502/503/504 as retryable and most other 4xx as terminal, but after X-litmus-b-024's text was corrected to the article's actual content (jitter and retry-storm anti-patterns, not a status-code retryability table), no fetched record here states that specific status-code breakdown, so it is carried as an unsourced note pending re-verification.

tools.name: Stripe (Idempotency-Key header)
tools.note: named production reference implementation of a client-generated idempotency key with a fixed 24-hour retention window. Not used by this repo.

evidence.text: Stripe stores idempotency keys for 24 hours.

evidence.quote: If Stripe receives two requests with the same key for the same endpoint within a 24-hour window, it returns the result of the first request rather than processing a second operation.

tools.name: AWS Durable Execution SDK
tools.note: documents at-least-once, not exactly-once, activity execution as the default reliability semantic a caller must design idempotency around. Not used by this repo.

evidence.text: The runtime guarantees that each activity runs at least once during an orchestration.

evidence.quote:
At-least-once per retry (default). The SDK initiates a START checkpoint and then
immediately runs the code inside the step without waiting for the checkpoint
response.

landscape.text: What separates this from ordinary service reliability is not the failure taxonomy -- timeouts, 5xx, throttling all still apply -- but what a retry re-executes. An ordinary idempotent retry resends the identical request and expects the identical answer; an agent's retried unit can re-run a non-deterministic model call that generates a different tool-call payload for the same logical intent on a second attempt, so the idempotency mechanism has to detect that case rather than assume it away: "A parameter fingerprint is stored, and mismatches are rejected rather than replayed" (X-litmus-c-011) -- a same-key, different-payload replay is a conflict to surface, not a request to silently execute either version of. Durable-execution platforms already build retry in at the activity level and say so plainly: "At-least-once per retry (default). The SDK initiates a START checkpoint and then immediately runs the code inside the step without waiting for the checkpoint response" (X-seam-dispatch-006), which is why at-least-once, not exactly-once, is the honest default and idempotency -- not retry avoidance -- is what turns repeated execution into one observable effect. Not every failure should even trigger a retry: "a failure category chooses the recovery action. Retry count is a detail inside one category" (X-xc-typed-errors-003), and unbounded retry is itself a documented failure mode: "Research shows that multi-agent systems fail at 41-86.7% rates in production without deliberate fault tolerance design" (X-xc-budget-006).

response.

usage.text: As a cross-cutting concern, reliability is applied at every step's own timeout/retry/backoff boundary rather than requested once by a caller -- the same posture this repo states for every cross-cutting guarantee: "Telemetry, policy, provenance and budget are applied by the platform, not requested by the caller" (F-b1-08). Concretely: a step carries its own idempotency key and payload digest before it runs (this repo's own adapter today is only 'key on the wire, no lease' -- F-b3-16, the weaker of the two shapes cap-idempotency's own contract distinguishes); a failed step is classified before any retry is attempted, since "a failure category chooses the recovery action. Retry count is a detail inside one category" (X-xc-typed-errors-003); the retry itself is bounded rather than open-ended, because "A bounded retry window forces the architecture to decide what happens after repeated unsuccessful attempts" (X-compose-loop-003); and the attempt carries its own cause class, backoff and attempt number as first-class state, per this repo's own proposed (and currently unbuilt) dispatch-level retry design.

gaps.what: idempotency-key-convention is cited in contract.standards by exactly two skills (cap-idempotency, seam-dispatch) as their governing standard, and named in the entities list of two more (cap-durable-execution, core-components), yet the entity's own KB source is exclusively F-b3-16 -- this repo's own PASS.md row -- with zero fetched research record behind it. Every research record touching the underlying IETF draft (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07), across eight separate record ids in this corpus, is status: search-only; none is status: fetched.
gaps.why_it_matters: A standard cited by two skills' formal contracts as the thing they conform to has never had its own specification text verified in this environment -- version, MUST/SHOULD language and scope all rest on search snippets, consistent with this repo's known page-fetch block (STATUS rows 14, 45), but that limit has not been separately flagged on this card until now.
gaps.research_query: can draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07 be fetched now, and does its text match what cap-idempotency's skill.json claims about MUST-uniqueness

gaps.what: Whether this repo's own idempotency design implements payload-fingerprint comparison -- the mechanism that catches a same-key, different-payload replay from a non-deterministic retry -- is unverified. F-b3-16 describes today's adapter as 'key on the wire, no lease', which names only the key, not a digest or fingerprint check; the fingerprint mechanism (X-litmus-c-011) is generic API-reliability guidance, not evidence about this repo's own implementation.
gaps.why_it_matters: Without a fingerprint check, a retried unit that regenerates a different tool-call payload under the same key would either silently execute the new payload or silently return the old result -- neither of which is the conflict-and-refuse behavior reliability for a non-deterministic unit requires.
gaps.research_query: does harness/dispatch or cap-idempotency's own conformance suite assert a same-key different-payload request is refused as a conflict

gaps.what: This repo's own architecture already names dispatch-level retry attempt as a state, but records its home_today as a gap: 'there are three implementations of dispatch and no contract between them, so a retry is whatever each one does.'
gaps.why_it_matters: Reliability's own sub-line names retries first; if each of the three dispatch adapters retries on its own terms, 'Reliability' as a cross-cutting concern has no single behavior to describe yet, only three uncoordinated ones.
gaps.research_query: kb_index.py search "seam-dispatch three implementations retry contract"

gaps.what: No harness or example in this repo demonstrates bounded retry, fingerprint-conflict detection, or backoff as a conformance-checked behavior. This card's 'planned' status is accurate and unqualified by anything measured.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every claim in this profile about how reliability should behave is sourced to external research or to this repo's own unbuilt architecture entities, not to a passing test; that distinction should not collapse once the card is later marked built.
